title: Active Recovery & Mobility - Vasaloppet Prep

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately. Sync movement with breathing - inhale on cow, exhale on cat. Focus on spinal articulation rather than speed.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Sit with hips flexed at 90 degrees. Gently switch legs, keeping torso upright. This targets hip mobility crucial for skiing endurance events. Move with control.

items.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Mobilization
items.cues: Pull toes toward shins with control. Hold briefly at top. Important for ski boot comfort and calf flexibility in long events.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg. Hold for 2 seconds. Keep core tight and hips level. Improves stability and balance needed for long-distance skiing.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Place forearms on wall at shoulder height, step forward until stretch is felt. Hold passively. Releases shoulder and arm tension from training.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Face wall, step one foot back, keeping heel down. Lean into wall gently. Hold without bouncing. Essential for ski-specific muscular tension relief.

items.name: Arch Hold
items.cues: Barefoot, curl toes to create arch dome without lifting toes off ground. Hold 3-5 seconds. Strengthens foot arch for better ski boot support and stability.

items.name: Adductor Rockbacks
items.cues: In wide-legged squat position, shift weight side to side gently. Keep chest upright. Opens hips and inner thighs - critical for skiing mechanics.

items.name: Child's Pose
items.cues: Kneel, sink hips to heels, extend arms forward. Breathe deeply and relax completely. Focus on parasympathetic recovery to lower heart rate.

rationale: User is returning from extended rest (999 days since last workout) and needs gentle re-acclimation. Recovery workout with RPE 3-4 is appropriate to rebuild movement patterns without excessive fatigue.
Training for 90km Vasaloppet ski race requires specific mobility and stability in hips, ankles, and feet. This session prioritizes these areas while maintaining low intensity.

Active recovery approach uses mobility and light movement to promote blood flow and adaptations without creating fatigue debt, allowing proper preparation for harder training ahead with 53 days until race.
